title.en: Lesson 1. The Two Faces of -(으)세요: Command & Honorific

blocks.md:
When you want to tell someone politely *“Please do this”*, attach **-(으)세요** to the verb stem:
- Stem without batchim → **-세요** *(가다 → 가세요)*
- Stem with batchim → **-으세요** *(앉다 → 앉으세요)*

**Remember the ㄹ rule from Stage 3?**
Stems ending in **ㄹ** drop the ㄹ: **만들다 → 만드세요**, **살다 → 사세요**!

**The Two Faces of -(으)세요**:

Most textbooks only teach this as a command, but in real Korean it has a second huge job:

1. **Polite command**: 여기 앉으세요. *(Please sit here.)*
2. **Honorific statement or question**: Describing what a respected elder or teacher does!
   - 선생님, 어디 **가세요**? *(Teacher, where are you going? / Not a command, just a respectful question!)*
   - 아버지는 지금 책을 **읽으세요**. *(Father is reading a book.)*

head: Verb
With -(으)세요
Meaning
rows: Please go / Where are you going?

items.tip: Please enjoy your meal. (Honorific for 먹다)
Teacher, where are you going? (Respectful question)

blocks.q: How do you attach -(으)세요 to 만들다 (to make)?
blocks.why: Remember the ㄹ rule: ㄹ drops before -(으)! 만들다 → 만드세요 (not 만들으세요).

blocks.q: In the sentence "선생님, 지금 어디 가세요?", what does 가세요 mean?
options: A polite question: "Where are you going?"
A past action: "Where did you go?"
blocks.why: -(으)세요 is not only for commands! When asking an elder or teacher, it politely asks about their action.
앉다 has a batchim, so it attaches -으세요: 앉- + -으세요 = 앉으세요.

blocks.hint: Verbs ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ before -(으)세요: 만들다 → 만드세요
blocks.why: ㄹ drops before -(으)세요: 만들다 becomes 만드세요.

blocks.md:
What is the difference between **앉으세요** and **앉아 주세요**?

- **-(으)세요** is a gentle directive: *“Please do X (for yourself or for courtesy).”*
- **-아/어 주세요** asks someone to do something **as a favor for you**: *“Please do X for my sake.”*

Conjugation follows the familiar vowel harmony of **-아/어서**:
- ㅏ, ㅗ → **-아 주세요** *(보다 → 봐 주세요, 돕다 → 도와주세요)*
- Rest → **-어 주세요** *(기다리다 → 기다려 주세요, 가르치다 → 가르쳐 주세요)*
- 하다 → **해 주세요** *(도와주세요, 전화해 주세요)*

head: Plain Command (-(으)세요)
Favor Request (-아/어 주세요)
Nuance Difference
rows: Please wait for me / do me the favor of waiting
Please look at this for me
Please help me! (돕다 is ㅂ irregular)

items.tip: Please wait for a moment (for me).
Please say that once more for me.

blocks.q: How do you ask "Please help me!" using 돕다 (ㅂ irregular)?
blocks.why: 돕다 is a ㅂ irregular verb: ㅂ turns to 와 before a vowel: 도와주세요!
When asking someone to wait for you as a favor, 기다려 주세요 is the natural choice.

blocks.hint: 하다 verbs conjugate to 해 주세요: 말하다 → 말해 주세요
blocks.why: 하다 becomes 해 주세요: 다시 한번 말해 주세요.

title.en: Lesson 3. Making Requests with Irregular Verbs (-아/어 주세요)

blocks.h: How Irregular Verb Stems Combine with -아/어 주세요
blocks.md:
To ask someone to do something for you politely, attach **-아/어 주세요** to the verb. Because it starts with **-아/어**, stem vowel rules and irregulars follow the same familiar patterns as **-아요/-어요**!

- **ㅏ / ㅗ vowels:** attach **-아 주세요** (닫다 → **닫아 주세요**, 보다 → **봐 주세요**).
- **Other vowels:** attach **-어 주세요** (읽다 → **읽어 주세요**, 쓰다 → **써 주세요**).
- **하다 verbs:** become **-해 주세요** (말하다 → **말해 주세요**).
- **ㄷ irregular:** ㄷ changes to ㄹ (듣다 → **들어 주세요**).
- **ㅂ irregular:** ㅂ changes to 우 (돕다 → **도와주세요**).
**도와주세요** is one compound word (no space) meaning “Please help!”, whereas most other verbs keep a space: **열어 주세요**, **들어 주세요**.

items.tip: Teacher, please call a taxi for me. (부르다 → 불러 주세요)
Please listen to my story until the end. (듣다 → 들어 주세요)
This is so heavy, please help me. (돕다 → 도와주세요)

blocks.q: How do you politely ask someone to listen using ‘듣다’ (to listen)?
blocks.why: 듣다 changes ㄷ to ㄹ before vowel endings: 들 + 어 주세요 → **들어 주세요**.

blocks.q: How do you ask someone to call a taxi using ‘부르다’ (to call)?
blocks.why: 부르다 is a 르-irregular verb: 부르 + 어 주세요 → **불러 주세요**.

blocks.q: Match each base verb with its correct polite request form.

blocks.meaning: The weather is hot, please turn on the air conditioner.
blocks.why: 틀다 has vowel ㅡ (not ㅏ/ㅗ), so it attaches -어 주세요: 틀 + 어 주세요 → **틀어 주세요**.

blocks.q: Conjugate 만들다 (to make) into a polite request for me: 「한국 음식을 ___ .」
blocks.why: 만들다 attaches -어 주세요: 만들 + 어 주세요 → **만들어 주세요**.

blocks.say: 길을 잘 모르겠는데 지도 좀 보여 주세요.
blocks.rom: gil-eul jal mo-reu-gess-neun-de ji-do jom bo-yeo ju-se-yo
blocks.q: Say it aloud politely asking to see a map.

title.en: Lesson 4. For Whom Is the Action: -(으)세요 vs -아/어 주세요

blocks.h: Beneficiary Makes the Difference: For Them vs For Me
blocks.md:
Both endings make polite sentences, but they have completely different purposes:

- **-(으)세요 (Do it for yourself / General directive):**
  - You are instructing or recommending the listener to do something for their own benefit:
  - 맛있게 **드세요** (Enjoy your meal / Eat well).
  - 편하게 **앉으세요** (Please take a comfortable seat).
- **-아/어 주세요 (Do it as a favor for me / Request):**
  - You are asking the listener to perform an action that **benefits you**:
  - 저 좀 **도와주세요** (Please help me).
  - 문 좀 **닫아 주세요** (Please close the door for me).

head: Verb
Directive / Honorific (-(으)세요)
Favor for Me (-아/어 주세요)
Contrast
rows: 앉아 주세요 (Please sit down for me)
봐 주세요 (Please take a look at my work)
써 주세요 (Please write it for me)

blocks.md: When asking a taxi driver to go to a destination, say **서울역으로 가 주세요** (favor for me), NOT 서울역으로 가세요 (which sounds like ordering the driver to go there alone!).

items.tip: Customer, please sit here comfortably. (Directive for listener's comfort)

items.ch: 회의 시작하니까 모두 자리에 앉아 주세요.
items.tip: The meeting is starting, so please take your seats. (Favor requested by speaker)
Please take a photo for me. (Favor benefiting speaker)

blocks.q: You are in a taxi and want the driver to take you to the airport. What do you say?
blocks.why: Taking you to the airport is a service/favor done for you, so use -아/어 주세요: **가 주세요**.

blocks.q: You invite a guest into your living room and want them to sit down comfortably. What do you say?
blocks.why: Telling a guest to sit comfortably for their own comfort is an honorable directive: **앉으세요**.

blocks.q: Match each situation to the most natural phrase.
pairs: Asking a friend to wait for you

blocks.meaning: Since it is cold, please close the door for me.
blocks.why: Asking someone to close the door for the room's comfort is a favor request: **닫아 주세요**.

blocks.q: Politely ask someone to teach you Korean (as a favor for you): 「제게 한국어를 ___ .」
blocks.why: Asking someone to teach you as a favor takes -아/어 주세요: 가르치다 → **가르쳐 주세요**.

blocks.say: 기사님, 명동역 3번 출구 앞에서 세워 주세요.
blocks.rom: gi-sa-nim, myeong-dong-yeog sam-beon chul-gu ap-e-seo se-wo ju-se-yo
blocks.q: Say it aloud politely asking a driver to stop at a location.
